proof_routes.reason: Opening enough data to recompute link(w) and link(r) gives binding, but it either reveals the link rows or moves the cost into a large opening proof.
A zero-knowledge circuit could prove committed preimages have the desired link relation, but that is a new proof system and is unlikely to beat a 68-byte account object without a concrete cost model.
A general byte hash digest does not supply add/scale operations or a response commitment equation.

requirements.reason: The byte-hash path can bind an opened encoded hidden state, assuming collision freedom and an injective encoding.
A digest of the full hidden preimage does not expose a committed quotient-link value or a verifier-checkable link projection.
The byte-hash commitment has no add/scale structure for checking link(z) = link(r) + c * link(w) on commitments.
The sampler surface is preserved only if link values remain hidden; opening them publicly reintroduces the public-link hiding failure.
Existing commitment binding can support an opening check, but does not by itself prove the hidden linear link equation.
No extra account bytes are needed only if reuse is free, but the missing non-public equation proof would add unknown proof bytes or assumptions.

summary.reason: Existing account commitments bind full hidden preimages only after opening; they do not expose a hidden quotient-link commitment or homomorphic link equation.  Any route that keeps the link hidden needs a new zero-knowledge/hash-circuit proof, and any route that opens link values reintroduces the public link hiding failure.
